quizzes.title: Straw Polls and Permanent Member Signals
quizzes.passage:
The Security Council has held a second round of informal straw polls to identify a potential successor to Antonio Guterres. His second term as UN Secretary-General is scheduled to conclude on 31 December 2026, so the selection is taking place as that date approaches. Straw polls form one stage in narrowing the field before the Council formally recommends a candidate to the United Nations General Assembly. Nominees also take part in interactive dialogues with Member States, where they discuss their vision for the United Nations and respond to questions from stakeholders.

During a straw poll, each Council member records a position on each candidate. The Council then studies the pattern of responses to see how each candidate is received. The polls are not the final decision, because the Council's recommendation is one part of a longer procedure that is completed when the General Assembly acts on it. The selection therefore unfolds in stages, with each stage building on the one before it. Guterres's term is the reason the process is taking place now, and the Council must work through each stage before a recommendation can be made. The booklet presents this as a key stage in the process, one that comes before any decision taken by the General Assembly.

questions.q: What does an Encourage indication mean in a straw poll?
options: The member supports or favours the candidate
The member has not taken a position
The member is requesting more nominees
questions.explanation: Encourage means the member supports or favours the candidate.

questions.q: What is the purpose of straw polls?
options: Selecting the host country for UN headquarters
Finalising the budget of the Secretary-General's office
Assessing the relative acceptability of candidates
questions.explanation: Straw polls assess the relative acceptability of candidates to Security Council members.

questions.q: Until when do straw poll rounds continue?
options: A fixed number of three rounds
Until a candidate demonstrates sufficient support
questions.explanation: Straw poll rounds continue until a candidate demonstrates sufficient support.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): A Discourage from a Permanent Member effectively signals a veto in a formal vote.
Reason (R): Permanent Members use distinctively coloured ballots, which makes it possible to identify whether a candidate is receiving opposition from a P5 member.
options: Both A and R are true, and R explains A
Both A and R are true, but R does not explain A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.explanation: Coloured ballots let the Council identify P5 opposition, which is why a Permanent Member's Discourage signals a veto.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about straw polls:
I. Straw polls are formal and binding votes.
II. Members may indicate Encourage, Discourage or No Opinion.
III. Permanent Members use distinctively coloured ballots in every round.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Straw polls are informal and confidential, and coloured ballots are used in subsequent rounds rather than every round.

questions.q:
How many of the following statements about straw polls are correct?
I. Straw polls are held only once before the Council recommends a candidate.
II. No Opinion means the member has not taken a position.
III. A Discourage from a Permanent Member means the candidate has been formally appointed.
questions.explanation: Only statement II is correct, since rounds are repeated and a Discourage signals a likely veto rather than an appointment.

questions.q: What do nominees typically submit as part of the nomination process?
questions.explanation: Candidates generally submit a curriculum vitae, vision statements and other relevant information.

questions.q: Which response indicates that a member supports or favours a candidate? (one word)

quizzes.title: UNSC Structure and the Veto
quizzes.passage:
The Council is responsible for maintaining international peace and security, and it is among the principal organs of the United Nations. The booklet describes the Council as the apex of that structure, which places it at the centre of the organisation's work. Its membership is arranged so that different members have different roles. Non-permanent members can set the agenda for meetings, and they can also lead various subsidiary bodies and working groups. Permanent Members have a distinct place in the Council, and the booklet treats their position as central to how decisions are reached.

The booklet argues that the Council's structure has not kept pace with the present world. It also connects the Council's current shape to the period in which the Council was created. For the Council to act on a matter, the arrangements that govern its decisions must allow a decision to pass, and the booklet examines whether those arrangements still serve the present international order. The discussion is therefore about how the Council is built, who sits in it, and how its decisions can be stopped or carried forward. The booklet also notes that the Council is part of the current process for choosing the next Secretary-General, which is why its procedures are being examined now.

questions.q: What happens when a single Permanent Member opposes a proposal?
options: The decision passes if a majority supports it
A unanimous vote of all UN members is needed
The decision is blocked regardless of other support
The matter is referred automatically to the ICJ
questions.explanation: Opposition from any one Permanent Member blocks a decision regardless of other support.

questions.q: Can a retiring Council member be re-elected immediately?
options: Yes, but only with a Permanent Member's vote
Yes, after a single term out of office
No, it is not eligible for immediate re-election
questions.explanation: A retiring member is not eligible for immediate re-election.

questions.q: Why did the five Permanent Members gain permanent membership?
options: They were the largest economies in the world
They won the Second World War
They founded the League of Nations
They were elected by the General Assembly
questions.explanation: The booklet states that the five Permanent Members gained permanent membership because they won the Second World War.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): The UNSC was powerless during the Russia-Ukraine conflict.
Reason (R): Russia used its veto as a Permanent Member.
options: Both A and R are true, and R explains A
Both A and R are true, but R does not explain A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.explanation: The UNSC was powerless because of Russia's veto, which a Permanent Member can use to block action.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the UN Security Council:
I. Each of the 15 members has one vote.
II. Non-permanent members hold veto power.
III. The General Assembly holds the veto power.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Only statement I is correct, since the veto belongs to the five Permanent Members.

questions.q:
How many of the following statements about the Security Council are correct?
I. The veto system is seen as a tool that can block progress in the UN.
II. A majority of members can override a Permanent Member's objection.
III. The five Permanent Members hold veto power.
questions.explanation: Statements I and III are correct, while statement II contradicts the rule that any one Permanent Member's opposition blocks a decision.

questions.q: The UNSC is one of how many principal organs of the UN?
questions.explanation: The UNSC is one of the six principal organs of the United Nations.

questions.q: Whose veto left the UNSC powerless during the Russia-Ukraine conflict? (name the country)
